intent: Understand why an unfamiliar practice or problem matters without becoming a specialist.
context: Intelligent reader with little prior knowledge of this article's technical or design domain.
desired_outcome: A clear mental picture and a reason to care that can be retold in ordinary language.
engagement_cues: Concrete examples and terms introduced when their meaning becomes necessary.
friction_cues: Insider shorthand that makes entry impossible, or a remedial lecture that stalls the story.
name: Curious outsider
invariants: Wants to understand why the subject matters without becoming a specialist.
Needs unfamiliar terms and practices introduced when they become useful.

variation_axes.description: The reader’s starting familiarity with the poll subject.

values.description: Little prior knowledge of the subject.
Understands a neighboring field or practice.
Knows common terms but not specialist detail.

variation_axes.description: How the reader prefers unfamiliar ideas to be made clear.

values.description: Needs examples before abstractions.
Uses a careful analogy as a bridge.
Can follow terms once briefly defined.

intent: Take one usable move from this article into a problem I already have.
context: Has a live task and little need for a complete philosophy of the subject.
desired_outcome: A next step with enough conditions to know when to try it.
engagement_cues: A concrete move, what it changed and the constraint that made it appropriate.
friction_cues: Insight that never becomes actionable, or a universal recipe detached from its case.
name: Practical borrower
invariants: Has a real problem and looks for a usable move.
Needs conditions that distinguish a suitable application from a universal recipe.

variation_axes.description: How soon the reader hopes to apply an idea.

values.description: Gathering ideas for a future task.
Working on a related task now.
Needs to make a near-term decision.

variation_axes.description: What form of practical takeaway best supports the reader.

values.description: A worked example to adapt.
A short sequence of checks.
A rule for choosing when to use an approach.

intent: Leave with a way to reason about similar decisions, not merely copy this solution.
context: Comfortable with complexity and interested in transferable distinctions.
desired_outcome: A decision rule that survives outside the author's exact circumstances.
engagement_cues: Competing options, governing constraints and why one consideration outranked another.
friction_cues: A list of tactics with no principle connecting them, or an aphorism with no test.
name: Model builder
invariants: Looks for distinctions that transfer beyond the current example.
Wants competing options and constraints connected to a defensible principle.

variation_axes.description: How much experience the reader has modeling interacting systems.

values.description: Understands examples better than abstract system models.
Can reason about connected parts and their effects.
Regularly builds or evaluates formal models.

variation_axes.description: How far beyond the immediate case the reader seeks a reusable idea.

values.description: Wants to adapt the move to a similar case.
Wants a rule that generalizes across contexts.
Wants a model for reasoning about a class of decisions.

intent: Test where the apparent lesson stops being true.
context: Enjoys a strong argument enough to push it against difficult cases.
desired_outcome: A claim whose boundaries become sharper under pressure.
engagement_cues: Visible assumptions, counterpressure and a concession that improves the argument.
friction_cues: A local success inflated into a rule for everyone.
name: Counterexample hunter
invariants: Tests where a promising claim stops being true.
Treats explicit limits as a way to sharpen an argument rather than weaken it.

variation_axes.description: The kind of pressure the reader first applies to a claim.

values.description: Looks for an exceptional case.
Tests the claim against common conditions.
Constructs a difficult opposing scenario.

variation_axes.description: What helps the reader decide whether a boundary is credible.

values.description: A causal explanation.
A contrast with a case where the claim fails.
A clear statement of where the claim does not apply.
